exposure: Breastfeeding status (at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months postpartum)
outcome: Proportion of women breastfeeding at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months postpartum
Disease-related factors (disease activity, self-reported health status via VAS scores for pain, fatigue, and total)
Medication use (conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs - csDMARDs)
Obstetric outcomes (pregnancy duration, cesarean section, premature birth)
cohort: The study included 227 women with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) who had 304 births, collected prospectively from the Norwegian nationwide quality register RevNatus.
finding: A high proportion of women with JIA breastfed at six weeks (86%) and six months (70%) postpartum, and breastfeeding women generally had higher education, longer pregnancy duration, lower prevalence of premature birth, and gave birth to newborns with a higher mean birth weight, along with lower VAS scores for pain, fatigue, and total health status six weeks postpartum.
mod_finding: Breastfeeding women had a lower prevalence of cesarean section (21% versus 45%, p-value 0.007) compared to non-breastfeeding women.
birth_weight: N/A (measured outcomes for breastfeeding vs non-breastfeeding groups were 3512 g vs 3175 g)
